about: print12: the print series of the book (6 x 9 in, standard colour, print on demand). series_title is THE ONE PLACE the series (and the online book) is named: tools/book/build_series.py uses it for the covers, title pages, running heads, copyright pages and the /book/ series block, and tools/book/build_book.py for the online book, its packages and PDFs. Change it, then rebuild (build_book.py, build_pdfs.js, build_series.py, BOOK_SERIES=1 build_pdfs.js). Chapters are the short versions, in the order given here. isbn fields stay empty until the owner buys ISBNs; an empty ISBN is simply not printed. examples: false leaves the filled-in examples out of the print books.

books.title: Know Yourself Kindly
books.sub: Where your lens came from, who you are now, and who you are becoming
books.line: Start with yourself: your history, your wiring, your feelings, your worth and what matters to you.
books.blurb: Before you can share a life well, it helps to know your own. This short book starts with you. Where did your way of seeing things come from: the home you grew up in, the old rules, the things life taught you? How are you wired today: your energy, your weather, the words that land and the ones that sting? And who are you becoming, one small step at a time? Along the way it explains how feelings work, why your worth is not a score, why personality is more like a set of dials than a box, and how to find what matters to you. Every chapter has everyday scenes, words you could use and one small thing to try this week. Nothing here is a test. Read it on your own, at your own pace.

books.title: Closer, Together
books.sub: Staying in tune, talking it through and mending what goes wrong
books.line: For any two people who share a life: pace and tone, stress, how words land, anger and repair.
books.blurb: Two people can care about each other and still fall out of tune. One wants to talk now; the other needs an hour. A comment meant lightly lands hard. A long day at work turns into a row about the dishes. This book is about the space between people, at home, in families, with friends or at work. It explains how pace and tone pull people apart, how stress changes what we hear, how communication really works, and why two people can see the same moment so differently. Then it turns to the hot minutes of anger, to repair and apologies that land, and to love in its many forms. Each chapter has everyday scenes, words you could use and one small thing to try. No blame and no verdicts: just a clearer view and a kinder next step.

books.title: Share the Load
books.sub: The work nobody sees, and a fair, kind way to share it
books.line: For homes, families and teams: seeing the unseen work, one owner per job, and two kinds of fair.
books.blurb: Every shared home, family or team runs on work that nobody sees: noticing the shoes are too small, booking the appointment, remembering bin day. When that work isn’t counted, someone ends up carrying more than anyone realises, and resentment grows quietly. This book helps you see the whole load, kindly and without keeping score. It shows a simple way to check whether the way you share the work can last, how much of a reaction is leftover stress, how to agree what fair means to each of you, and a gentle monthly look-back that catches what weekly chats miss. It ends with helping others well without burning out. Each chapter points to a workpaper that puts it to use, free to print from the website. It looks at the setup, never at the person.

books.title: Understanding People
books.sub: How trust, change, loss, minds and groups work, for anyone
books.line: How people work: belonging, change, grief, minds that work differently, worry and groups.
books.blurb: Why do we need each other so much? Why is change so hard, even when we want it? How does grief move, and what helps? This book explains how people work, in plain words and with everyday examples. It covers belonging and trust, habits and change, loss and big life changes, minds that work differently (autism, ADHD, sensory and learning differences), worry and low mood, and the pull of the groups we belong to. It ends with an afterword that draws the threads of the whole series together. Each chapter has words you could use, common mix-ups and something small to try, for anyone, in any kind of relationship. Where a chapter touches hard things, it says where to find help. Read it in order, or start wherever you need it today.

workbook.title: The Workpapers: Free Forms, All in One
workbook.sub: Every workpaper from the series, on big pages, to fill in by hand
workbook.line: All the workpapers on large pages, with room to write and spare copies for the weeks ahead.
workbook.blurb: Every workpaper from the Spread Love & Acceptance books, on big pages with room to write. Inside are blank copies of all ten: a quick check of how much you’re carrying, a calm-down kit you make on a calm day, a self-check before you reply to something that stung, a 90-second daily check-in, a one-week log of who did what, a list that gives every job one owner, a monthly look-back, and more. Each one starts with a short page that says when to use it, how long it takes, who fills it in and which book explains it. Then come spare copies for the weeks ahead, a planner for the six-week program and pages for your own notes. The sheets describe what happened, never who someone is. Every form is also free to print or fill in online; this book simply puts them all in one place.
